Rather than assign integer labels to our data, we use it to create new binary columns to represent our categories. Before we would transform one original column into one transformed column but in this case, we will transform one column into several transformed columns, one per category. One-hot encoding creates new binary columns to represent our categories. If we have 𝑐 categories in our column, we create 𝑐 new binary columns to represent those categories. - Example: Imagine a language column which has the information on whether you - We can use sklearn's `OneHotEncoder` ::: --- ## How to one-hot encode ::: {#82068f8a .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} X_toy ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=9} ```{=html}
